ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a regular pentagon, with point O marked inside and representing the center. The shaded region is in the lower right part of the pentagon; its boundary includes the line segment from O to the upper right vertex, the right outer side, part of the bottom side, and the perpendicular line segment drawn downward from O to the bottom side; a right-angle mark is also drawn at the bottom side. Reasoning: Connecting the center O respectively to the five vertices of the regular pentagon can divide the pentagon into 5 congruent central triangles, so each central triangle accounts for 1/5 of the whole pentagon. The shaded part contains one complete central triangle on the right side. In addition, the perpendicular from O to the bottom side in a regular polygon will bisect that side, so the small piece near the bottom side in the shading is exactly half of the adjacent bottom central triangle, namely 1/2 × 1/5 = 1/10. Therefore the shaded area accounts for 1/5 + 1/10 = 3/10 = 30% of the whole pentagon.

raw_record.question_text: The point $O$ is the centre of a regular pentagon. How much of the pentagon is shaded?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a regular pentagon with centre O. The shaded region is bounded by the segment from O to the upper-right vertex, the right outer side, part of the bottom side, and the perpendicular segment from O to the bottom side. Split the regular pentagon by joining O to all five vertices; this makes 5 congruent central triangles, each one-fifth of the pentagon. From the image, the shaded region contains one whole central triangle on the right, plus half of the adjacent bottom central triangle because the perpendicular from the centre to a side of a regular polygon bisects that side. Therefore the shaded fraction is 1/5 + 1/2·1/5 = 3/10 = 30%.
